key_insight: Serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) distinguished traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI), supporting its potential as an injury-specific neurotrauma biomarker.
clinical_relevance: If validated, blood-based BD-tau testing could support early neurotrauma differentiation, triage, and injury-specific trial enrollment.
method: Measured baseline serum BD-tau in multiple cohorts comprising 285 TBI patients, 57 SCI patients, and 22 controls.
Compared injury-type discrimination with paired cerebrospinal fluid measurements and established blood biomarkers.
Tracked serum BD-tau trajectories up to 144 hours after injury.
evidence_signal: Serum BD-tau distinguished TBI from SCI with an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.96) overall and outperformed established blood biomarkers in a comparison analysis (AUC 0.82 versus 0.53–0.71; all DeLong p<0.001).
watch_item: Findings from neuro-intensive care cohorts require validation in broader acute-care populations, including patients with concurrent brain and spinal cord injuries.
paper_title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
